group.title: Arts and books
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A long written story about invented people and events.
wrong: A novel is a short poem of four lines.

words.meaning: A person who writes books.
examples: The {author} signed copies of her book.
wrong: The author is the person who reads the book.

words.meaning: The events that form the story of a book or film.
examples: The film has a very clever {plot}.
wrong: The plot is the color of the book cover.

words.meaning: A type of art, music or writing, like horror or jazz.
wrong: A genre is the name of one actor.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to give opinions on books, films or art.
examples: The {critic} gave the play five stars.
wrong: A critic is a person who never gives opinions.

words.meaning: A work of art made from stone, wood or metal.
examples: There’s a bronze {sculpture} in the square.
wrong: A sculpture is a song for the piano.

words.meaning: A painting, drawing or photo of a person.
examples: A {portrait} of the queen hangs in the hall.
wrong: A portrait is a painting of a mountain with no people.

words.meaning: A view of land, or a painting of it.
wrong: A landscape is a painting of a person’s face.

words.meaning: The act of playing music, acting or dancing for an audience.
examples: Her {performance} in the play was amazing.
wrong: A performance is a private practice with no audience.

words.meaning: A practice before a public performance.
wrong: A rehearsal is the last show after everything ends.

words.meaning: A person who writes plays.
wrong: A playwright is a child who plays games.

words.meaning: A person who controls how a film or play is made.
examples: The {director} told the actors where to stand.
wrong: The director is the person who sells tickets.

words.meaning: One part of a play or film in one place.
wrong: A scene is the music in a film.

words.meaning: The music of a film.
examples: I love the {soundtrack} of that movie.
wrong: A soundtrack is the list of actors.

words.meaning: The words of a song.
examples: I don’t know the {lyrics} of this song.
wrong: Lyrics are the notes a piano plays with no words.

words.meaning: A person who writes music.
wrong: A composer is a person who only listens to music.

words.meaning: A large group of musicians who play together.
wrong: An orchestra is one person singing alone.

words.meaning: A film or TV program that gives facts about real events.
wrong: A documentary is an invented story with dragons.

words.meaning: A film made from drawings or computer images that move.
wrong: Animation is a film with only real actors and no drawings.

words.meaning: A book or film that continues an earlier story.
examples: The {sequel} was even better than the first film.
wrong: A sequel comes before the first film in the story.

words.meaning: The first public showing of a film or play.
wrong: The premiere is the last show after years of performances.

words.meaning: To prepare and print a book or article for sale.
examples: Her book will be {published} next year.
wrong: They published the book, so nobody can buy it.

words.meaning: One of the parts of a book.
examples: I read the first {chapter} last night.
wrong: A chapter is a whole library of books.

words.meaning: A book about someone’s life, written by another person.
wrong: A biography is a book about invented animals.

words.meaning: Stories about imaginary people and events.
wrong: Fiction is only true facts about real events.

words.meaning: Poems as a type of writing.
wrong: Poetry is a type of math.

words.meaning: A picture in a book.
wrong: An illustration is a page of text with no pictures.

words.meaning: A sale where things go to the person who offers the most money.
examples: The painting sold at {auction} for a million dollars.
wrong: At an auction, the lowest offer always wins.

words.meaning: All the actors in a play or film.
examples: The {cast} took a bow at the end.
wrong: The cast is the people who watch the play.

words.meaning: A room where an artist works, or where films or music are made.
examples: The band recorded the album in a {studio}.
wrong: A studio is a field where cows live.

words.meaning: A work of art of the highest quality.
examples: Many think this painting is his {masterpiece}.
wrong: A masterpiece is his worst and weakest work.

words.meaning: Belonging to the present time.
wrong: Contemporary art is from five hundred years ago.

words.meaning: Writing stories and poems using imagination.
wrong: Creative writing means copying a phone book.

words.meaning: A book that sells a very large number of copies.
examples: Her new novel is already a {bestseller}.
wrong: A bestseller is a book nobody buys.

words.meaning: The sound of people clapping.
examples: The singer was met with loud {applause}.
wrong: Applause is the silence after a bad show.

words.meaning: The raised area where actors and musicians perform.
wrong: The stage is where the audience sits.

words.meaning: To act, sing or play music for an audience.
wrong: She performed by staying at home in silence.

words.meaning: To show something in public, like art in a museum.
wrong: They exhibited the paintings by hiding them.

words.meaning: Making things by hand with skill.
wrong: A craft is a machine that makes everything for you.

words.meaning: The history, traditions and buildings of a country.
examples: The old town is part of our cultural {heritage}.
wrong: Heritage is something built last week with no history.
